reviews.title: Compelling but I have suggestions
reviews.text:
I've switched from Covenant Eyes to Migiri because it contains features that I find a bit more useful. I do have a couple of questions / suggestions though (This was sent as a support email, but I thought I'd drop it here too)

1. I was wondering if there was an ability to add multiple people as companions. If not,   then I suggest considering adding this ability. Being able to develop a community of fellow recoverers or accountability partners can be extremely powerful. I for one have multiple friends in mind who I'd love to have as companions.

What would be even better would be to develop some sort of social function from within the app, similar to Covenant Eyes. Then, friends would be able to see each other's progress from within the app itself (perhaps even with the ability to receive notifications) rather than having to check their email, which in all honesty is usually bloated and not checked very often by people these days, especially with the younger generation, myself included.

2. I don't quite understand the 'Protection Mode' function. 

Under 'Preferences > App Uninstall Protection > Protection Mode', I saw that you have the ability to enable a feature where your companion's approval is needed in order to disable & uninstall Migiri. However, it seems to me that this feature is essentially useless because you can just as easily switch it back to "Hard" mode & then wait the 24 hour request period. It would make more sense if, once switched to "Companion" mode, one would need the companions approval in order to switch it back to "Hard" mode. 

If this is the particular reason for not allowing multiple companions, the issue could be solved by allowing the user to assign one of their companions a sort of "primary status." This "primary" companion would be responsible for approving functions like this and any similar functions potentially added to the app in the future. 

I really hope that your developers find these suggestions compelling. This is coming from the mind of a fellow addict who's trying to improve your app for the betterment of everyone using it, which will also drive more people to switching like I have. I'd love to see a response from your team letting me know if I can hope to see anything like these suggestions in future updates or just any thoughts at all. Thank you.

reviews.title: Do NOT try the free trial
reviews.text:
I signed up for a free 7-day trial on their website, and upon discovering that the app offers little more than an illustrated rowboat timeline of days gone without porn, I deleted the app—but I made the mistake of not canceling the trial before my 7 days was up. 

They proceeded to charge me $159.99 for a full year subscription. I immediately began emailing support, offering to pay for one month as penance for my oversight. They finally replied after one week, saying they will “consider reviewing my case” since it is an “unusual circumstance” in which I forgot to cancel the free trial that clearly stated I’d be charged for a full year at the end of the 7 days. 

This is a dishonest company blatantly engaging in predatory sales tactics, counting on a percentage of you to try their “free trial” and forget to cancel so that they can legally mug you.

reviews.title: UPDATED REVIEW:  App does not work & Delete Prevention can be disabled before deleting the app
reviews.text:
This app does NOT block porn as stated and does not prevent the user from deleting from the installed device. I was able to delete this within seconds by simply changing certain settings first before deleting entirely. All you have to do is turn off Migiri’s access in the ‘Screen Time’ settings and you can delete the app w/o issue. Apple, nor Migiri, seem to care about the fake and fraudulent service that is being offered at a ridiculous annual price of $160+tax. 

When following directions for a refund, I was told to contact Apple, which is not what the website states, when seeking a partial refund. 

To all who struggle with this addiction and are looking for help in your battle for freedom, keep looking beyond this app because it gives a false sense of support and doesn’t actually do what it explicitly states it will. Buyer beware.
